body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal I_{\mathcal R_T,x}(\mu_x)=[\min_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathcal R_T}(\mu_x)}\mathsf N(\gamma)/\mathsf S(\gamma),\ \max_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathcal R_T}(\mu_x)}\mathsf N(\gamma)/\mathsf S(\gamma)]\), with the finite-strata analogue obtained by replacing numerator and denominator by \(\sum_x\omega_x\mathsf N(\gamma_x)\) and \(\sum_x\omega_x\mathsf S(\gamma_x)\). Under \(\mathcal R_T^{\uparrow}\), this equals \([H_-(\mu),H_+(\mu)]=[\frac{\sum_d(\ell_d-a_d)_+}{\sum_d\min\{u_d,\max\{\ell_d,a_d\}\}},\frac{\sum_db_d}{\sum_d\max\{\ell_d,b_d\}}]\).

sampling_model.design: Conditional Bernoulli random assignment satisfies \(Z\perp(D^{\mathrm{pot}},Y^{\mathrm{pot}})\mid X\) and \(0<P(Z=1\mid X=x)<1\) on a finite nonempty covariate support. The no-covariate ordered formulas are the singleton-stratum case.
sampling_model.units: An independent and identically distributed sample of participants with observed \(W=(Z,D,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) and finite covariate \(X\). Conditional arm-state vectors \(\mu_x\) index the fixed-stratum programs, and \(\omega_x=P(X=x)\) indexes finite-strata aggregation.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary randomized assignment may change both selection and the positive selection layer. The researcher chooses finite linear restrictions \(\mathcal R_{T,x}\) on the conditional response-type masses. KMV Strong Monotonicity \(D_1\ge D_0\) is one such submodel; a protocol-controlled algorithm that may retain or upgrade but not downgrade assigned tiers is one design supporting it, not a requirement of the broader theorem.
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional assignment overlap holds in every reported stratum. The general response-type target additionally requires the observable lower bound \(\inf_{(\gamma_x)}\sum_x\omega_x\mathsf S(\gamma_x)\ge\kappa>0\); under Strong Monotonicity this becomes \(\sum_d\ell_d\ge\kappa\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For fixed finite \(L\) and finite \(\mathcal X\), the primitives are empirical conditional arm-state probabilities and empirical stratum weights. Identification requires no smoothing or learned nuisance; conditional inference with sparse strata is a separate implementation issue.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Remark 2(i) lists \(D_1\ge D_0\) as Strong Monotonicity inside the researcher-chosen linear response-type restrictions \(\mathcal R_T\), and Theorem 1 gives sharp multilayer outcome bounds in that general response-type framework.

Accessible arXiv v6 Proposition 2 gives sharp conditional probability-of-causation bounds for the always-observed subgroup under conditional random assignment, positive mass, and monotone binary sample selection; journal proposition identity was not independently verified.
Theorem 2 gives a closed sharp interval for the fraction negatively affected using Fr\'echet bounds on observed treatment-arm marginals.

Proposition 5 and equations (7)--(8) give sharp Fr\'echet bounds for benefit across ordered outcome categories without outcome monotonicity, with tiered harm obtained by reversing the ordered-category comparison.
The directional delta method applies to Hadamard directionally differentiable maps, and valid resampling estimates the directional derivative rather than bootstrapping a nonlinear map naively.
A shrinking finite-difference evaluation consistently estimates the law of a directionally differentiable transform pointwise.
Calibrated projection delivers confidence intervals for projections of partially identified parameters with uniform asymptotic validity.
Aggregated conditional linear-program support values are regular under a margin condition and admit root-\(n\) Gaussian inference.

body.tldr: Conditional random assignment identifies the arm-specific layer--outcome margins but not the joint response type, same-positive-layer stayer mass, or harm among those stayers. For any finite set of KMV linear response-type restrictions \(\mathcal R_T\), an expanded-state flow polytope gives sharp conditional harm-fraction endpoints as two explicit Charnes--Cooper linear programs, with an exact decoder and a finite-strata aggregate obtained by weighting numerator and denominator by \(P(X=x)\). KMV Remark 2(i) already includes \(D_1\ge D_0\) as Strong Monotonicity; the genuine closed-form contribution is the binary-harm collapse in that submodel: the stayer diagonal is a Cartesian box, the joint stayer--harm region is an exact prism, and its ratio contracts to sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints with an observable iff certificate for unavoidable harm. A protocol-controlled retain-or-upgrade tier design is one credibility example, not the source or claimed novelty of Strong Monotonicity.

project_justification.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal provide the governing multilayer response-type framework, explicitly list Strong Monotonicity among the admissible researcher-chosen restrictions, and derive sharp mean-effect bounds under general linear response-type restrictions. Existing probability-of-causation and harm results do not characterize binary harm within latent same-positive-layer stayers when both the harm numerator and stayer denominator depend on an unidentified multilayer response table. Nor do they give the all-layer Cartesian diagonal projection and closed-form ratio contraction under Strong Monotonicity.
project_justification.niche: The lead result extends the KMV response-type program from conditional means to the binary fraction harmed among same-layer stayers: at fixed \(X=x\), two explicit finite linear programs give the exact sharp interval for any finite linear \(\mathcal R_T\), including Lee monotonicity with movements in both directions among positive layers. The finite-strata target aggregates the flow numerator and denominator with observable weights \(P(X=x)\).
project_justification.fill: An exact expanded-state decoder proves sharpness for the general response-type programs. Under KMV Strong Monotonicity, strict-triangular residual transport yields the Cartesian diagonal box, simultaneous binary-outcome completion yields the joint hinge prism, and a coordinatewise fractional contraction yields the displayed \(O(L)\) endpoints and the unavoidable-harm iff certificate.

body.related_work: Kroft, Mourifi\'e, and Vayalinkal supply the anchor response-type framework. Their June 3, 2026 version treats restrictions on response-type probabilities as researcher-chosen linear constraints \(\mathcal R_T\); Remark 2(i) explicitly includes \(D_1\ge D_0\) as Strong Monotonicity, and Theorem 1 applies within that framework. Accordingly, this paper does not claim to introduce or supply the first support for ordered-layer monotonicity. Its broader result is a binary-harm extension: for any finite linear \(\mathcal R_T\), including Lee monotonicity alone with both directions among positive layers, the harmed-stayer fraction has sharp endpoints given by two explicit linear programs. Its distinctive closed-form result is the collapse under KMV Strong Monotonicity to an all-layer Cartesian diagonal box, an exact joint hinge prism, and an \(O(L)\) ratio formula. The protocol-controlled retain-or-upgrade design remains only a credibility example. Possebom and Riva give sharp one-always-observed-stratum probability-of-causation bounds; Kallus gives sharp harm bounds from observed arm outcome marginals; and de Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp benefit and harm bounds across ordered outcome categories. Those results inform binary outcome coupling but do not identify the multilayer same-stayer response table or its unidentified-denominator ratio. The expanded-state transport and Charnes--Cooper steps are standard finite-dimensional optimization machinery and carry no novelty claim. Fang--Santos and Hong--Li provide the directional and numerical delta framework, while Kaido--Molinari--Stoye provide projection-inference precedent; the remaining pointwise numerical-delta verification at simultaneous ties and structural zeros is separate from the identification theorems proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For a general linear response-type restriction \(\mathcal R_T\), the exact result is a pair of finite linear programs after Charnes--Cooper scaling; no general closed form is claimed. The \(O(L)\) formulas, Cartesian diagonal box, and layerwise prism rely on KMV Strong Monotonicity \(D_1\ge D_0\). That restriction is researcher chosen and is neither validated nor point-identified by arm margins, although KMV provide its formal precedent and a protocol-controlled retain-or-upgrade design can make it credible. The positive-stayer floor is maintained because otherwise the conditional ratio can be undefined. Fixed-\(L\), finite-strata identification includes zero observable cells, but this solve does not establish uniform numerical-delta validity across local sequences crossing ties; exact confidence-set image projection remains the robust fallback.
body.honest_scope: The paper's broad deliverable is a sharp binary harmed-stayer characterization for any finite KMV linear response-type restriction, conditional at fixed \(X=x\), with a finite-strata aggregate and two explicit linear programs. The generic decoder and fractional linearization are tools, not novelty claims. The specialized contribution under KMV Strong Monotonicity is the exact Cartesian diagonal box, simultaneous stayer--harm prism, linear-time closed-form ratio contraction, and observable iff certificate for unavoidable harm, all valid at structural zero cells. KMV already provide the Strong Monotonicity restriction and general response-type framework; protocol-controlled tier assignment is only one substantive rationale for selecting that submodel. No closed form is asserted for Lee monotonicity alone or arbitrary reciprocal positive-layer movement. No claim is made about total welfare, empirical rejection of zero harm, growing \(L\), continuous covariates, semiparametric efficiency, or uniform numerical-delta inference near changing active sets.
body.interpretation: At a fixed \(X=x\), the target is the probability of a binary loss under treatment among units whose positive selection layer would be identical under both assignments. It is not the total fraction harmed in the population, a mean treatment effect, or harm among everyone selected in both arms. The finite-strata target first sums the harmed-stayer and stayer masses using \(P(X=x)\) and then takes their ratio; it is not an unweighted average of stratum-specific ratios.
